title: Angles & angle chasing
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Write every angle you find on your sketch. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are $[[a]]^\circ$ and $[[b]]^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?

mistakes.why: The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$, not $360^\circ$.

hints: The three angles add to $180^\circ$.

problems.prompt: An isosceles triangle has a top angle (between the two equal sides) of $[[x]]^\circ$. What is each base angle, in degrees?

mistakes.why: $[[x]]^\circ$ is the angle between the equal sides, so it appears once. The two base angles share $180 - [[x]]$.

hints: The two base angles are equal and add to $180 - [[x]]$.

problems.prompt: An exterior angle of a triangle is next to one interior angle. The other two interior angles are $[[a]]^\circ$ and $[[b]]^\circ$. What is the exterior angle, in degrees?

mistakes.why: That is the interior angle next to it. The exterior angle is the sum of the two far interior angles.

hints: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it.

problems.prompt: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $[[p]] : [[q]] : [[s]]$. What is the largest angle, in degrees?
hints: There are $[[p + q + s]]$ equal parts in $180^\circ$.
problems.solution: One part is $\frac{180}{[[p + q + s]]} = [[180/(p + q + s)]]$, so the largest angle is $[[s]] \times [[180/(p + q + s)]] = [[180*s/(p + q + s)]]$.

problems.prompt: Lines $\ell$ and $m$ are parallel, and a third line crosses both. Two angles lie between $\ell$ and $m$ on the same side of the third line. One of them is $[[x]]^\circ$. What is the other, in degrees?

mistakes.why: These co-interior angles are not equal: they add to $180^\circ$.

hints: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to $180^\circ$.

title: Angle chasing challenge
instructions: Five AMC-style problems with choices (A) to (E), easiest first. You can leave a problem blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each problem.

problems.prompt: One angle of a triangle is $50^\circ$ and another is $65^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?
An exterior angle of a triangle is $120^\circ$, and one of the two interior angles not next to it is $45^\circ$. What is the other one, in degrees?

why.A: The two far interior angles add to the exterior angle.

problems.prompt: An isosceles triangle has an angle of $100^\circ$. What is the size of one of its other angles, in degrees?

why.E: Two angles of $100^\circ$ would add to more than $180^\circ$.

problems.solution: The $100^\circ$ angle must be the top angle, so each base angle is $\frac{180 - 100}{2} = 40$, choice (B).

problems.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$ and $\angle A = 36^\circ$. The bisector of $\angle B$ meets $AC$ at $D$. What is $\angle BDC$, in degrees?

figure.alt: Triangle ABC with A at the top, AB equal to AC and a 36 degree angle at A. A segment from B meets side AC at D.

why.E: That is $\angle ADB$, the angle on the other side of $D$.

problems.solution: $\angle B = \angle C = \frac{180 - 36}{2} = 72$, so $\angle ABD = 36$. $\angle BDC$ is an exterior angle of triangle $ABD$: $36 + 36 = 72$, choice (C).

problems.prompt: The five points of a five-pointed star are formed by drawing all five diagonals of a convex pentagon. What is the sum of the five angles at the tips of the star, in degrees?

why.E: That is the angle sum of the pentagon itself.

problems.solution: Pick one tip. Its two lines and the segment joining two other tips make a triangle. Each of that triangle's other two angles is an exterior angle of a small triangle, so it equals the sum of two more tips. So the five tip angles fill exactly one triangle: $180^\circ$, choice (B).

title: Pythagoras & special right triangles
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Square the legs, add, then take the square root. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has legs $[[(3 + 2*t)*k]]$ and $[[(4 + 8*t)*k]]$. How long is the hypotenuse?

mistakes.why: Don't add the legs. Add their SQUARES, then take the square root.

hints: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$. Look for a multiple of $3, 4, 5$ or $5, 12, 13$.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has hypotenuse $[[c]]$ and one leg $[[a]]$. How long is the other leg? (A square root is fine.)

mistakes.why: $[[c]]$ is the hypotenuse, the longest side: subtract, $[[c]]^2 - [[a]]^2$.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has two legs of length $[[x]]$. How long is its hypotenuse?

mistakes.why: Use Pythagoras: the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{[[x]]^2 + [[x]]^2} = [[x]]\sqrt{2}$.

hints: In a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{2}$ times a leg.

problems.prompt: In a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle the shortest side is $[[x]]$. How long is the other leg?

mistakes.why: That is the hypotenuse. The longer leg is $\sqrt{3}$ times the shortest side.

hints: The sides are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$.
problems.solution: The longer leg is $[[x]]\sqrt{3}$ (and the hypotenuse is $[[2*x]]$).

problems.prompt: An equilateral triangle has side $[[s]]$. What is its height?

mistakes.why: The height splits the base in half: use $\frac{[[s]]}{2}$ as the short leg.

hints: The height cuts the triangle into two $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangles with short leg $[[s/2]]$.

title: Pythagoras challenge
instructions: Five AMC-style problems with choices (A) to (E), easiest first. You can leave a problem blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each problem.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has legs $6$ and $8$. How long is the hypotenuse?

why.D: Add the squares of the legs, not the legs.

problems.prompt: A rectangle is $5$ by $12$. How long is its diagonal?
A square has a diagonal of length $10$. What is its area?

why.E: That is the diagonal squared. The square's area is half of it.

problems.solution: The side is $\frac{10}{\sqrt{2}}$, so the area is $\frac{100}{2} = 50$, choice (C).

problems.prompt: An equilateral triangle has side $8$. What is its area?
problems.solution: The height is $4\sqrt{3}$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 4\sqrt{3} = 16\sqrt{3}$, choice (B).

problems.prompt: A right triangle has perimeter $30$ and hypotenuse $13$. What is its area?
problems.solution: The legs add to $17$ and $a^2 + b^2 = 169$. Then $2ab = 17^2 - 169 = 120$, so the area $\frac{ab}{2} = 30$, choice (B).

title: Similar triangles
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Match the sides that face equal angles, then use one ratio. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: A pole $[[h]]$ m tall casts a shadow $[[s]]$ m long. At the same moment a tree casts a shadow $[[t]]$ m long. How tall is the tree, in metres?

mistakes.why: Keep the same order on both sides: height over shadow for the pole equals height over shadow for the tree.

hints: The sun's rays make similar triangles: $\frac{\text{height}}{\text{shadow}}$ is the same for both.

problems.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, $D$ is on $AB$ and $E$ is on $AC$ with $DE$ parallel to $BC$. If $AD = [[a]]$, $DB = [[b]]$ and $DE = [[d]]$, how long is $BC$?

mistakes.why: Compare with the WHOLE side $AB = [[a + b]]$, not $DB$.

hints: Triangle $ADE$ is similar to triangle $ABC$ with ratio $\frac{AB}{AD} = \frac{[[a + b]]}{[[a]]}$.

problems.prompt: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio $[[p]] : [[q]]$. The smaller has area $[[w]]$. What is the area of the larger?

mistakes.why: Areas scale by the SQUARE of the side ratio: $\left(\frac{[[q]]}{[[p]]}\right)^2$.

hints: If sides are multiplied by $k$, areas are multiplied by $k^2$.

problems.prompt: Two similar triangles have areas $[[a]]$ and $[[a*k*k]]$. A side of the smaller one is $[[s]]$. How long is the matching side of the larger one?

mistakes.why: The areas grew by $[[k*k]]$, so the sides grew by $\sqrt{[[k*k]]} = [[k]]$.

hints: Side ratio $= \sqrt{\text{area ratio}}$.

problems.prompt: The altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle splits the hypotenuse into pieces of length $[[p]]$ and $[[p*m*m]]$. How long is the altitude?

mistakes.why: That is the average of the pieces. The altitude is their geometric mean: $h^2 = pq$.

hints: The altitude makes two smaller triangles similar to each other, so $\frac{h}{p} = \frac{q}{h}$.

title: Similar triangles challenge
instructions: Five AMC-style problems with choices (A) to (E), easiest first. You can leave a problem blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each problem.

problems.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $DEF$, with $AB = 4$, $BC = 6$ and $DE = 10$. How long is $EF$?
A person $6$ feet tall casts a shadow $4$ feet long. At the same time a flagpole casts a shadow $20$ feet long. How tall is the flagpole, in feet?
In triangle $ABC$, $DE$ is parallel to $BC$ with $D$ on $AB$ and $E$ on $AC$. If $AD = 3$, $DB = 6$ and $DE = 4$, how long is $BC$?

figure.alt: Triangle ABC with A at the top. Segment DE joins a point D on AB to a point E on AC and runs parallel to the base BC.

why.A: Compare with the whole side $AB = 9$, not $DB = 6$.

problems.prompt: Two similar triangles have perimeters $12$ and $18$. The smaller one has area $20$. What is the area of the larger one?

why.A: Areas scale by the square of $\frac{3}{2}$, not by $\frac{3}{2}$.

problems.solution: The scale factor is $\frac{18}{12} = \frac{3}{2}$, so the area is $20 \times \frac{9}{4} = 45$, choice (C).

problems.prompt: A right triangle has legs $6$ and $8$. How long is the altitude to the hypotenuse?

why.E: Remember the $\frac{1}{2}$ in the area: $24 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times h$.

problems.solution: The area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24$ and the hypotenuse is $10$, so $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times h = 24$ and $h = \frac{24}{5}$, choice (B).

title: Area
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Half base times height, with the height square to the base. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: A triangle has a base of length $[[b]]$ and a height of $[[h]]$ to that base. What is its area?

mistakes.why: That is the rectangle. A triangle is half of it: $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.

hints: Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.

problems.prompt: An isosceles triangle has sides $[[5*k]]$, $[[5*k]]$ and $[[6*k]]$. What is its area?

mistakes.why: The slanted side $[[5*k]]$ isn't the height. Drop the height to the base: it is $[[4*k]]$.

hints: The height to the base $[[6*k]]$ splits it into halves of $[[3*k]]$. Use Pythagoras with $[[5*k]]$.
problems.solution: The height is $\sqrt{[[5*k]]^2 - [[3*k]]^2} = [[4*k]]$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \times [[6*k]] \times [[4*k]] = [[12*k^2]]$.

problems.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has area $[[w]]$. Point $D$ is on $BC$ with $BD : DC = [[p]] : [[q]]$. What is the area of triangle $ABD$?

mistakes.why: $ABD$ gets $[[p]]$ of the $[[p + q]]$ equal parts of the base: $\frac{[[p]]}{[[p + q]]}$.

hints: Triangles $ABD$ and $ABC$ have the same height from $A$, so their areas compare like their bases.

problems.prompt: The midpoints of the three sides of a triangle with area $[[w]]$ are joined to make a smaller triangle. What is its area?

mistakes.why: Its sides are half as long, so its area is $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}$ of the big one.

hints: The three lines cut the triangle into $4$ matching triangles.
problems.solution: The midpoint triangle is one of $4$ equal pieces: $\frac{[[w]]}{4} = [[w/4]]$.

problems.prompt: A triangle has sides $[[13*k]]$, $[[14*k]]$ and $[[15*k]]$. What is its area?
hints: Heron's formula: $s$ is half the perimeter, and the area is $\sqrt{s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)}$.

title: Area challenge
instructions: Five AMC-style problems with choices (A) to (E), easiest first. You can leave a problem blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each problem.

problems.prompt: What is the area of the triangle with corners $(0, 0)$, $(8, 0)$ and $(3, 5)$?
A triangle has sides $5$, $12$ and $13$. What is its area?

why.D: It is a right triangle: half the product of the legs.

problems.solution: $5^2 + 12^2 = 13^2$, so the legs are $5$ and $12$: $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30$, choice (B).

problems.prompt: A triangle has sides $7$, $8$ and $9$. What is its area?
Triangle $ABC$ has area $60$. $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. What is the area of triangle $BDE$?

why.E: That is triangle $ABD$. $E$ halves it again.

problems.solution: The median $AD$ halves the area: $ABD$ is $30$. $BE$ is a median of $ABD$, so $BDE$ is $15$, choice (C).

problems.prompt: A triangle has sides $10$, $10$ and $12$. How long is the altitude to one of the sides of length $10$?

why.B: That is the altitude to the base of length $12$.

problems.solution: The altitude to the base is $\sqrt{100 - 36} = 8$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 8 = 48$. Then $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times h = 48$ gives $h = \frac{48}{5}$, choice (C).

title: Polygons & angle sums
instructions: Type each answer and press Check. Angle sum $180(n - 2)$; exterior angles add to $360$. Stuck? Open a hint.

problems.prompt: What is the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with $[[n]]$ sides, in degrees?

mistakes.why: Split the polygon into triangles from one corner: you get $[[n - 2]]$ triangles, not $[[n]]$.

hints: From one corner, diagonals split an $n$-gon into $n - 2$ triangles.

problems.prompt: What is each interior angle of a regular polygon with $[[n]]$ sides, in degrees?

mistakes.why: That is the exterior angle. The interior angle is $180 - [[360/n]]$.

hints: Each exterior angle is $\frac{360}{[[n]]}$.
problems.solution: Exterior angle $\frac{360}{[[n]]} = [[360/n]]$, so the interior angle is $180 - [[360/n]] = [[180 - 360/n]]$.

problems.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is $[[180 - e]]^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
hints: Each exterior angle is $180 - [[180 - e]] = [[e]]$, and they add to $360$.

problems.prompt: How many diagonals does a polygon with $[[n]]$ sides have?

mistakes.why: Each diagonal joins two corners, so counting from every corner counts it twice. Divide by $2$.

hints: From each corner, diagonals go to all corners except itself and its two neighbours: $[[n - 3]]$.

problems.prompt: A regular hexagon has side $[[s]]$. What is its area?

mistakes.why: That is one equilateral triangle. A regular hexagon is made of six of them.

hints: Split the hexagon into $6$ equilateral triangles of side $[[s]]$; each has area $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}[[s]]^2$.

title: Polygons challenge
instructions: Five AMC-style problems with choices (A) to (E), easiest first. You can leave a problem blank. Your answers are marked when you hand in the set, and you'll see a worked solution for each problem.

problems.prompt: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon, in degrees?
Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is $24^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
A polygon has $20$ diagonals. How many sides does it have?
The interior angles of a convex polygon add up to $2340^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
$ABCDE$ is a regular pentagon. What is $\angle ACD$, in degrees?

why.E: That is the whole angle at $C$. Take away $\angle BCA$.

problems.solution: Each interior angle is $108$. Triangle $ABC$ is isosceles with $AB = BC$, so $\angle BCA = \frac{180 - 108}{2} = 36$. Then $\angle ACD = 108 - 36 = 72$, choice (C).

title: Warm-up for the check
instructions: Five quick problems, one from each lesson. Type each answer and press Check. Hints are here, but not in the check.

problems.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are $[[a]]^\circ$ and $[[b]]^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?

mistakes.why: The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$, not $360^\circ$.

hints: The three angles add to $180^\circ$.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has two legs of length $[[x]]$. How long is its hypotenuse?

mistakes.why: Use Pythagoras: the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{[[x]]^2 + [[x]]^2} = [[x]]\sqrt{2}$.

hints: In a $45$-$45$-$90$ triangle the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{2}$ times a leg.

problems.prompt: A pole $[[h]]$ m tall casts a shadow $[[s]]$ m long. At the same moment a tree casts a shadow $[[t]]$ m long. How tall is the tree, in metres?

mistakes.why: Keep the same order on both sides: height over shadow for the pole equals height over shadow for the tree.

hints: The sun's rays make similar triangles: $\frac{\text{height}}{\text{shadow}}$ is the same for both.

problems.prompt: A triangle has a base of length $[[b]]$ and a height of $[[h]]$ to that base. What is its area?

mistakes.why: That is the rectangle. A triangle is half of it: $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.

hints: Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.

mistakes.why: Split the polygon into triangles from one corner: you get $[[n - 2]]$ triangles, not $[[n]]$.

title: ⭐ Unit 11 check
instructions: Eight AMC-style problems with choices (A) to (E), easiest first, no hints. You need all 8 right to pass. Each try gives you different problems.

problems.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are $47^\circ$ and $68^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?

why.D: That is $47 + 68 - 2$. Subtract both angles from $180$.

problems.prompt: The angles of a triangle are $x^\circ$, $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and $(3x - 10)^\circ$. What is the largest angle, in degrees?

why.A: That is $x$. Put it back into each angle.

problems.solution: $6x = 180$, so $x = 30$ and the angles are $30$, $70$ and $80$, choice (D).

problems.prompt: An isosceles triangle has a top angle (between the two equal sides) of $[[x]]^\circ$. What is each base angle, in degrees?

why.B: $[[x]]^\circ$ is the top angle, not a base angle.
why.D: The two base angles SHARE what is left.

problems.prompt: A right triangle has legs $8$ and $15$. How long is the hypotenuse?

why.D: Add the squares, not the legs.

problems.prompt: A $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle has hypotenuse $10$. What is its area?

why.C: Remember the $\frac{1}{2}$: the legs are $5$ and $5\sqrt{3}$.

problems.solution: The legs are $5$ and $5\sqrt{3}$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 5\sqrt{3} = \frac{25\sqrt{3}}{2}$, choice (A).

problems.prompt: A $13$-foot ladder leans against a wall with its foot $5$ feet from the wall. The foot slides out until it is $12$ feet from the wall. How many feet does the top slide down?

why.B: That is how high the top ends up. Subtract from where it started.

problems.solution: At first the top is $\sqrt{169 - 25} = 12$ feet up; afterwards $\sqrt{169 - 144} = 5$. It slides $7$ feet, choice (C).

problems.prompt: A rectangle has a diagonal of length $10$ and a perimeter of $28$. What is its area?
problems.solution: The sides add to $14$ and their squares to $100$. So $2ab = 196 - 100 = 96$ and $ab = 48$, choice (C).

problems.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $DEF$, with $AB = 6$, $DE = 9$ and $AC = 8$. How long is $DF$?
Two similar triangles have matching sides $3$ and $5$. The smaller one has area $18$. What is the area of the larger one?
Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $C$. The altitude $CD$ meets the hypotenuse at $D$, with $AD = 4$ and $DB = 9$. How long is $CD$?

why.E: That is $CD^2$. Take the square root.
why.C: That is the average of the pieces. The altitude is their geometric mean.

problems.prompt: A triangle has base $12$ and height $7$. What is its area?
A triangle has sides $13$, $14$ and $15$. What is its area?
Square $ABCD$ has side $6$, and $M$ is the midpoint of side $CD$. What is the area of triangle $ABM$?

why.A: The height from $M$ to $AB$ is the full side, $6$.

problems.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has area $60$. $D$ is on $BC$ with $BD = 2 \cdot DC$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$. What is the area of triangle $BDE$?
problems.solution: $ABD$ has $\frac{2}{3}$ of the area, $40$. $BE$ is a median of $ABD$, so $BDE$ is $20$, choice (C).

problems.prompt: What is each interior angle of a regular decagon (10 sides), in degrees?
problems.solution: Each exterior angle is $36$, so each interior angle is $144$, choice (D).

problems.prompt: How many diagonals does a polygon with $[[n]]$ sides have?

why.B: Each diagonal was counted from both ends.

problems.prompt: A regular hexagon has side $4$. What is its area?

why.A: A hexagon is six equilateral triangles; each has area $4\sqrt{3}$.

problems.prompt: The interior angles of a convex polygon add up to $1800^\circ$. How many diagonals does it have?
$ABCDEF$ is a regular hexagon with side $2$. How long is the diagonal $AC$?

figure.alt: A regular hexagon ABCDEF with side 2. The diagonal from A to C is drawn.

problems.solution: Triangle $ABC$ has sides $2$, $2$ and an angle of $120$ between them. Its height from $B$ is $1$, so half of $AC$ is $\sqrt{4 - 1} = \sqrt{3}$ and $AC = 2\sqrt{3}$, choice (C).
